items.label: The railway journey as an adventure

slides.title: Where we stand today
body: Bookings have returned to pre-2020 volume in every European market, but the shape of demand has changed. Shorter trips, later decisions, and far more mobile.

slides.title: Rail is winning the long weekend
bullets: Three-day trips up 18% year on year
Booking window has shortened to 21 days
Half of all bookings now start on a phone
Winter demand now spills into March

slides.title: What the numbers tell us about products
bullets: Panoramic Roundtrip stays the anchor product at 8 days and 7 nights
**Gran Train Tour** outsells every other package in the UK market
Group bookings recovered to 2019 levels in Zürich and Stuttgart
Hong Kong remains below plan and needs a separate campaign
London recovered fastest once direct rail connections returned

slides.title: How partners actually sell us
left: Agents rarely sell a route. They sell a picture of a day: a window seat, a pass, and something warm at the end of it. The itinerary matters less than the promise that nothing will need to be organised on arrival.
That is why the packages that travel best are the ones with the fewest decisions left open.
right: The counter-argument we hear most often is price. In practice the objection is rarely the total; it is the absence of a comparison. When a partner can put the rail package beside the equivalent self-drive week, the conversation ends quickly.

right.text: Our job for 2026 is to supply that comparison, in the partner's own language, before they are asked for it.

slides.title: Two ways people travel with us

right: The second group buys a week off. They arrive through a partner, they decide late, and they want one confirmation email that covers everything.
